## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sanniṭṭhāpakattheraapadāna* is a verse biographical text located in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya (designated as Tha Ap 46) [SuttaCentral]. Like other poems in this collection, it preserves the spiritual autobiography of an elder disciple (*thera*), recounting meritorious deeds in past lives and their fruits culminating in awakening. The SuttaCentral database records five translations of the text in five modern languages, without providing a distinct translated English title [SuttaCentral].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan traditions [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates considerable Pali-internal reuse, identifying 31 matching passages shared across 11 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partner is the first part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (10 matches, notably aligning segments 1.4–2.4) [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares extended conventional verse patterns with several other *Therāpadāna* compositions, including the *Kilañjadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 236, segments 5.4–9.1 matching 3.4–7.1), the *Tālavaṇṭadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 219, segments 5.1–7.3 matching 4.1–6.3), the *Ekavandaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 232), the *Rahosaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 137), and both texts entitled *Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 104 and Tha-Ap 130) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
